findings.quote: The one exception is HL, which is SSA in a right triangle.
findings.problem: False absolute. HL is not the only time SSA proves congruence. When the given angle is obtuse or right, or more generally when the side across from the given angle is at least as long as the other given side, only one triangle can be built, so two triangles with those matching parts are congruent. Example: an angle of $120^\circ$ with the side $5$ next to it and the side $8$ across from it fixes one triangle. A student taught that HL is the one exception will wrongly reject such a pair.
findings.source: Checklist B01; reader rules, Added after the Sol audit (test every 'only' and stated rule); SSA ambiguous-case analysis, verified by construction (the circle of radius $8$ about the far vertex meets the ray from the $120^\circ$ vertex once), as also taught in content/lessons/mathematics/trigonometry/laws-of-sines-and-cosines.md, #3: The Ambiguous Case (SSA)

findings.quote: (SSA works only as HL in a right triangle)
findings.problem: The trap warning repeats the same false absolute with 'only'. SSA also proves congruence when the given angle is obtuse, or when the side across from the given angle is the longer of the two given sides. The warning tells the student this never happens outside a right triangle.
findings.source: Checklist B01; reader rules, Added after the Sol audit; same SSA ambiguous-case analysis as the finding above

findings.quote: Its corners are right angles, because the two acute angles of each triangle add to $90^\circ$.
findings.problem: The proof does not explain how it works without its picture, and the picture is an ILLUSTRATION placeholder that the app does not show. The prose never says how the four triangles sit (each side of the big square split into $a$ and $b$), why the middle shape has sides $c$ (each is a hypotenuse), or why a $90^\circ$ sum of the acute angles makes the corner $90^\circ$ (the corner and the two acute angles lie on a straight side, so they add to $180^\circ$). The brief lists 'Prove the Pythagorean theorem' as absent at curriculum class, so the student must be able to follow this proof.
findings.source: Checklist L26 (and L23: prose teaches without the image); lesson style guide, Illustration placeholders (placeholders are invisible in the app); brief, upcat-L191
